children: After diving nearly 6%, CBOT corn futures have managed to cut some losses with most-active futures now down 4.7% to $4.91 a bushel. The WASDE showed a larger-than-expected corn production outlook, counter to what analysts anticipated. Market conditions have primed corn for further selling ahead, says Dave Toth of StoneX in a note. "It is highly likely that the extent of today's plunge is due at least in part to the overall market forcing the capitulation of this long-&-wrong exposure," says Toth. "Further meltdown should not surprise. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
